description: Corrections found by checking contests against a named source. Each record names the imported file, the source that shows the right figures, and why. The raw file stays as imported; scripts/build-test2-election-manifest.mjs (applySourceCheckedFixes) lays the operations over it at build time and shows the reason in the contest's 'Corrected' note. Operations: set {path, value}; candidate {name, set}; addCandidate {row}; replaceCandidates {candidates}.

batches.ni-and-dail-2026-10-18: Northern Ireland local government 1973-2011, the 1996 Forum (Belfast East) and two 2014 Dáil by-elections, checked against ARK Northern Ireland Elections, Wikipedia and ElectionsIreland.org.
batches.roi-local-2026-10-18: Irish local elections checked against IrelandElection.com (the independent check) and ElectionsIreland.org (the site Civgraph's figures were first taken from): winners not marked as elected, seat counts, quotas, and contests imported with no candidates or no votes, filled only where every candidate has a first preference that adds up to the page's valid poll and the winners equal the seats. Fills for 1974, 1979 and 1985 apply when those years are published.
batches.dail-byelections-2026-10-18: Dáil by-elections 2009-2021 imported with second-count figures as first preferences, missing candidates or a stray row, checked against ElectionsIreland.org and Wikipedia.
batches.official-records-2026-10-23: Results contradicted by official membership records: Dáil winners and Ceann Comhairle automatic returns (Houses of the Oireachtas, with ElectionsIreland.org and Wikipedia), NI Assembly and Westminster winners (NI Assembly, UK Parliament), and 2014 and 2019 council candidates the import left named 'Party' (ARK Northern Ireland Elections, Democracy Club, CC BY 4.0).
batches.eoni-2014-2026-10-26: Northern Ireland local council election of 22 May 2014, every contest checked candidate by candidate and stage by stage against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's result sheets as published on Open Data NI (Open Government Licence).
batches.eoni-wayback-2026-10-26: Northern Ireland council contests checked against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's own result sheets and results booklets, retrieved from the Internet Archive's copies of eoni.org.uk. Figures from the scanned booklets were read from the page images, not taken from OCR, and confirmed by the site owner.
batches.ni-council-xref-2026-10-27: Northern Ireland council contests 1973-2011 cross-checked against ARK's per-contest result spreadsheets (Nicholas Whyte, ark.ac.uk), the Wikipedia council election articles and the quota each result sheet states (the valid poll divided by one more than the seats, rounded down, plus one).
batches.person-id-splits-2026-10-28: Candidates of the same name in different councils that the imported data gave one Candidate_Id, and so one person record. Each council's candidate is given an id of their own; within a council they stay together until a source says otherwise.
batches.candidate-id-splits-2026-10-28: The imported Northern Ireland council data gave every candidate of one name the same Candidate_Id in every council, joining different people into one. Each such id keeps the council where it is used most; elsewhere each council's candidate gets an id of their own ('<id>-<council>'). Nothing in the results changes.
batches.gallagher-1923-first-prefs-2026-10-28: First-preference figures for the August 1923 Dail election taken from Michael Gallagher, Irish Elections 1922-44: Results and Analysis (1993), where the imported figures did not add up to the valid poll.
batches.gallagher-1922-44-counts-2026-10-29: Count tables for 1922-44 Dail contests taken from Michael Gallagher, Irish Elections 1922-44: Results and Analysis (1993), where the imported data had none or only first preferences (count sidecars in data/elections/dail-wikipedia-counts named as Gallagher's), with the figures and names his tables show to be wrong in the imported data corrected. Figures read from the page images.
batches.ni-dea-names-2026-10-29: Northern Ireland council contests 1973-2011 in Newry and Mourne, North Down, Newtownabbey (1985), Coleraine and Limavady (1989) that were shown under their import spreadsheet names, named as ARK Northern Ireland Elections and the electoral-area maps name them.
batches.party-labels-2026-10-29: Party labels corrected: Dail candidates of June 1927 (National League), 1943-44 (Clann na Talmhan) and 1944-48 (National Labour) shown as Independents, checked against Gallagher's Irish Elections 1922-44, Wikipedia and the Houses of the Oireachtas; Michael Sheehan (Cork Borough 1948) and Thomas O'Hara (Mayo North 1951-57) shown as Fine Gael; and two Unionist Party of Northern Ireland candidates of October 1974 shown as Ulster Unionists, from the nomination notice.
batches.ark-crosscheck-2026-10-29: Disagreements between ARK Northern Ireland Elections (Nicholas Whyte) and Civgraph settled against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's result sheets and results booklets (Internet Archive copies).
batches.ie-crosscheck-fills-2026-10-30: Contests imported with no candidates, filled from ElectionsIreland.org result pages, Gallagher's Irish Elections 1922-44, and the Department's official local election results books and council count sheets; cross-checked against IrelandElection.com.
batches.ie-crosscheck-corrections-2026-10-30: Disagreements between IrelandElection.com and Civgraph (shifted figures, winners, first preferences) settled against official results books and count sheets, Gallagher's Irish Elections 1922-44, and ElectionsIreland.org.
batches.rte-2024-locals-2026-10-30: 2024 local election contests checked against RTÉ's published count results.
batches.party-labels-followup-2026-10-30: Follow-up to party-labels-2026-10-29: the agreed Ailtirí na hAiséirghe and Clann Éireann relabels and a source note for Patrick O'Reilly (Cavan 1943, 1944). Stage only; merge with the usual tool. mergeAction 'append' where source-checked-fixes.json already holds a record for that sourceFile (party-labels-2026-10-29).
batches.ark-six-contests-2026-10-30: Six NI Assembly (1973, 1982) and Convention (1975) contests the ARK cross-check of 2026-10-29 left out for want of an official sheet, settled from the Chief Electoral Officer for Northern Ireland's published result sheets (eoni.org.uk, Internet Archive copies of 1 April 2017). Includes 1982 Belfast South and 1975 Belfast East, settled from the same sheets.
batches.ni-booklets-sweep-2026-10-30: Every remaining 1973 Assembly, 1975 Convention and 1982 Assembly contest checked against the Chief Electoral Officer for Northern Ireland's published result booklets (eoni.org.uk, Internet Archive copies of 1 April 2017): header figures, first preferences and the members elected. The six contests of ark-six-contests-2026-10-30 and its two further records are in that batch.
batches.elliott-qub-2026-10-31: Queen's University of Belfast general elections of 1949, 1953 and 1958 checked against Sydney Elliott, Northern Ireland Parliamentary Election Results 1921-1972 (Political Reference Publications, 1973), with the Wikipedia article on the constituency as the second source: Samuel Irwin (UUP), elected first at all three, was missing, so a defeated candidate showed as elected each time. Applied only where both sources agree.
batches.elliott-1921-labour-2026-10-31: Belfast Labour Party candidates at the Northern Ireland general election of 24 May 1921 relabelled Independent Labour, as Sydney Elliott, Northern Ireland Parliamentary Election Results 1921-1972 (Political Reference Publications, 1973), prints them; Graham Walker's account agrees.
batches.stormont-flags-2026-10-31: Stormont contests flagged in 2026-10-31 review: vote totals that failed the turnout check (Cromac 1953, Oldpark 1933, Pottinger 1945, Londonderry City 1945 and 1947) and 25 contests the import showed unopposed although both reference works print an electorate. Checked against B. M. Walker, Parliamentary Election Results in Ireland 1918-92 (RIA 1992) and David Boothroyd's Northern Ireland House of Commons results (Internet Archive), with contemporary Belfast and Derry newspapers (British Newspaper Archive) for the five vote-total flags and Falls 1942.
batches.strabane-belfast-1961-bna-2026-10-31: Strabane Urban District Council 1899-1967 and the Belfast Corporation election of May 1961, checked against the newspaper reports in the British Newspaper Archive (Derry Journal, Londonderry Sentinel, Londonderry Standard, Strabane Chronicle, Tyrone Constitution, Northern Whig, Belfast News-Letter, Belfast Telegraph): misread names, figures and party labels, the poll figures of three 1958 wards, and contests imported with no result.
batches.stormont-names-2026-11-01: Stormont names and members corrected after the Belfast Gazette cross-check: titles and Wikipedia qualifiers written into names, a party label imported as a name, North Londonderry 1933 and 1938, and the 1938 Windsor poll.
batches.site-fixes-2026-11-01: Fixes found while preparing the promotional video: the 1918 Westminster returns for King's County and Cork City checked against the Irish Republican Digital Archive's copy of The Irishman (14 December 1918) and the Dáil-keyed copy of the same contests, and Parnell's 1880 Meath label checked against Walker's printed table.
batches.ina-newspapers-2026-11-01: Republic of Ireland contests checked against newspaper reports read in the Irish Newspaper Archives (OCR text, page images where noted): Dail by-election first preferences that the papers add up to the printed valid poll, presidential election dates and second counts, Republic local-election figures, and 35 1979 and 1985 local contests imported with no candidates, transcribed from the county papers' count reports. Facts and citations only.
batches.bna-westminster-2026-11-01: Westminster by-elections in Ireland, 1885-1922, checked against newspaper reports in the British Newspaper Archive; figures changed only where the page image was read or the printed majority confirms the figure. Facts and citations only.
batches.gazette-names-2026-11-01: Stormont members' names where the Belfast Gazette's return of members differed from Civgraph, each settled with a second source (another Gazette return, Wikipedia's article on the member) before changing anything.
batches.party-research-2026-11-02: Party labels settled 2026-11-02 against Walker's Parliamentary Election Results in Ireland (1978 and 1992 volumes), the official Dáil results of 1981 and February 1982, ARK Northern Ireland Elections, Elliott and Flackes (1999) and the Irish Republican Digital Archive: the Workers' Party's earlier names (Official Sinn Féin, Sinn Féin The Workers' Party, Republican Clubs), 'Republican Clubs' removed from 1935-66 Westminster Republicans, Provisional Sinn Féin's seven February 1982 candidates, the 1981 H-Block prisoner candidates, four 1981 council independents, Republican Sinn Féin candidates imported as independents, and the 1880 Parnellites shown as Home Rule. Printed labels kept in Party_As_Printed; inferred labels carry partyInferred and partyBasis. Stage only; merge with the usual tool. mergeAction 'append' marks a sourceFile that already has a record.
batches.person-identity-splits-2026-11-02: Candidacies filed under the wrong person, found while verifying official person ids and duplicate people for the parliamentary votes work. Each operation gives the candidacy the person id of the man it belongs to (a Wikipedia article, a History of Parliament page, an ElectionsIreland or IrelandElection.com candidate id), or a fresh candidate id where he has none, so the registry rebuild stops joining him to a namesake. Nothing in the results changes.
batches.result-corrections-2026-11-02: Result rows corrected against the History of Parliament and Wikipedia's election boxes (which cite Walker and Stooks Smith): a winner's name, a candidate wrongly marked elected, a by-election candidate's name.
batches.belfast-gazette-1970-winners-2026-11-03: Members returned at the 18 June 1970 Westminster election in Northern Ireland, from the Belfast Gazette (issue 2635, 8 July 1970): the 12 results had no winner marked.
batches.elliott-flackes-1999-2026-11-06: Northern Ireland contests 1968-99 checked against Sydney Elliott and W. D. Flackes, Northern Ireland: A Political Directory 1968-1999 (Blackstaff Press, 1999), read from the owner's scans, with every changed figure or label confirmed by a second source (ARK Northern Ireland Elections, Wikipedia): Chichester-Clark's 1970 Londonderry vote and Sands's April 1981 vote, Faulkner's seven pro-Assembly Unionists of February 1974, Kilfedder's 1979 Independent Unionist label, Dunlop's 1982 and the 1977 council UUUP candidates, the Ballymena and Larne 1977 unopposed returns, Larne's 1973 Loyalists, Ballymoney Town 1989, and candidacies filed under a namesake (Jack Allen, William Brown, John Carson, Gerry Kelly, John Kelly, Frank Millar junior, David Allen, P. J. Bradley and five 1996 Forum list rows). Facts and citations only.
batches.ledger-eoni-ec-2026-11-11: Northern Ireland council (2014, 2023) and European Parliament (2004) contests checked against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's result sheets and the Electoral Commission's results spreadsheets: only clear transcription errors (an electorate, poll or quota that the sheet's own figures confirm, a count total, the elected flags).
batches.galway-city-2026-11-11: Galway City West 2024, imported with no candidates, filled from Galway City Council's official State of the Poll sheets (counts 1-14), with IrelandElection.com person ids.
batches.two-member-unopposed-2026-11-11: Two-member county seats imported as single-member: both members were returned unopposed, but the second was shown as defeated. Checked against Walker (1978) as Wikipedia's election boxes cite it, and corroborated by the second member's own votes in the next session (Historic Hansard).
batches.roi-local-index-2026-11-11: Irish local election gap-fills that were on file but never reached the site, because their areas were missing from the election index (2014, 2019 and 2024): each fill was re-checked against the Department's results book for that year (candidates, first preferences, parties, members elected, seats, valid poll and quota) and the total poll added from the same book.
batches.roi-local-2024-book-2026-11-11: Irish local elections of 7 June 2024 checked against the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage's Local Elections 2024: Results, Transfer of Votes and Statistics (the book and its spreadsheet, on opendata.housing.gov.ie): the 21 areas imported with no candidates and no fill are filled from it, and where a contest on file disagrees with the book (a first preference, a member elected, a party label, the electorate or other poll figures) the book's figure is taken and the old one named. Every area's count-by-count result is in data/elections/roi-local-counts/2024-06-07/. Where the book contradicts itself the figure its own arithmetic or its county totals give is used, and the note says so.
batches.eoni-ia-2026-11-11: Northern Ireland Assembly 2011 and council 2011 contests checked against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's result sheets recovered from the Internet Archive (the old eoni.org.uk site's /getattachment/ and root-level files): only figures the sheet's own arithmetic confirms (first preferences that add up to the valid poll, stage totals that reconcile with the transfers and non-transferable votes).
batches.review-eoni-wikidata-2026-11-11: Northern Ireland contests checked against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's result sheets, turnout tables and declarations and the Electoral Commission's results spreadsheets: the EU referendum 2016 electorates, rejected-paper counts for the Assembly 2007 and 2011 and Westminster 2005, a missing 2010 electorate, elected flags the declarations confirm, and the Westminster 2017 East Londonderry rejected count, where the Electoral Commission's itemised figure is preferred to the Electoral Office's web page.
batches.arith-audit-2026-11-11: Every contest's arithmetic audited (scripts/check/rules/contest-arithmetic.mjs): FPTP votes against the valid poll, STV quotas, first preferences, stage-by-stage transfers and exclusions, turnout and poll figures. Figures that did not add up were checked against the source each record names and corrected where Civgraph had mis-transcribed them; where the source itself does not add up, the contest is listed in contest-arithmetic-allowlist.json instead.
batches.eoni-review-2026-11-11: Northern Ireland council contests of 2011 and 2019 checked by eye, figure by figure, against the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's scanned result sheets and result workbooks recovered from the Internet Archive (the 2011 council sheets and the 2019 sheets of Belfast, Derry City and Strabane, Lisburn and Castlereagh and Newry, Mourne and Down that the eoni-ia sweep could not machine-read). A figure is corrected only where the sheet's own arithmetic confirms it: each stage's transfers reconcile with the surplus or exclusion and the non-transferable votes, and each stage sums to the valid poll. Where a count is rebuilt (replaceCountRows) its stage totals keep the fractions the sheet prints.
batches.w8-review-2026-11-12: Northern Ireland council contests of 2014, 2019 and 2023 whose stage totals the import had cut to whole votes: the totals rebuilt from the transfers (restoreStageFractions) were each read by eye on the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's scanned result sheet (w8-review, 12 Nov 2026), where OCR had not found them; contests where any rebuilt total differs from the sheet are not included.
batches.w8-arith2-2026-11-12: Contests that still failed the contest arithmetic check (scripts/check/rules/contest-arithmetic.mjs) after arith-audit and w8-arith, checked against their sources: for the Northern Ireland councils of 1973-2005, the Electoral Office's declaration sheets (its Local Government Election Results booklets) and Nicholas Whyte's ARK spreadsheets transcribing them; for the Dail, ElectionsIreland.org's count sheets and the official results. A figure is changed only where the source shows it and the corrected stage then reconciles (each transfer brings the stage total to the next, and the votes handed out match the surplus or the votes of the candidates excluded). Where the source's own figures do not add up, the contest is listed in contest-arithmetic-allowlist.json instead.
batches.gap-roi-2026-11-12: Republic of Ireland local contests that Civgraph held with no candidates, filled from an official results book read by eye or from a newspaper's printed first count (Irish Newspaper Archives), with IrelandElection.com as the pointer and for full names: a record is added only where the source's first preferences add up to the valid poll and the elected equal the seats (gap-roi, 12 Nov 2026). Each reason says what was read where.
batches.review-rest-2026-11-12: Northern Ireland council counts of 2014, 2019 and 2023 whose transfers differed from the Electoral Office for Northern Ireland's scanned result sheet (w8-review's list, 12 Nov 2026), and contests that still failed the contest arithmetic check: each sheet was read by eye, cell by cell, and the count rows set to the sheet's transfers and stage totals (candidateCount, or replaceCountRows where a non-transferable row was missing), so that every stage's transfers add up to the surplus or the votes excluded and every stage sums to the valid poll. Where the sheet's own figures do not add up, the contest is allowlisted in contest-arithmetic-allowlist.json with the reason (review-rest, 12 Nov 2026).

source.title: B. M. Walker (ed.), Parliamentary Election Results in Ireland, 1918-92 (RIA 1992), p. 58; Belfast News-Letter, 7 Nov 1942

records.reason: There was one Falls by-election in 1942, polled on Friday 6 November 1942 and counted on Saturday 7 November. Richard Byrne (N) died on 28 August 1942 (Stormont Hansard 1942, list of members), so no Falls contest could have been held on 2 April 1942; the 2 April date comes from Wikipedia's by-election list. Walker p. 58 and Boothroyd date it 6 Nov 1942; Belfast Telegraph and Northern Whig of 6 Nov 1942 report polling 'to-day', the Belfast News-Letter of 7 Nov reports it 'yesterday', and Hansard records Donnelly as elected 7 November 1942 (declaration). Votes as held (Donnelly 4,595, McGouran 1,971, Glass 1,821) agree with every source; 40 spoilt papers, electorate 17,633 (Belfast News-Letter, 9 Nov 1942, p. 4). Walker prints R (Republican). The candidates stood as abstentionist republicans; no party organisation is named for them.

The History of Parliament (1820-1832, Wexford, and its entries for both brothers) gives the 1830 member as William Wigram (1780-1858); Sir Robert had sat for Wexford only from June 1829 to March 1830.
